facts.why: A doctor can find out what is wrong and give the right medicine. Rest and water help your body recover.
facts.can: Say three things you should do when you feel ill.
facts.summary: When you feel ill, see a doctor, take the right dose of medicine on time, and rest and drink water.

questions.prompt: When you feel ill, what should you do FIRST?
questions.explain: A doctor finds out what is wrong and gives the right medicine.
options: Only sleep and do nothing else
Buy any medicine from a pharmacy without advice
questions.answer: See a doctor

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a good idea when you are ill?
questions.explain: Leftover medicine may be wrong or unsafe — never take it.
options: Rest more and drink plenty of water
Take the right amount of medicine on time
Take leftover medicine from last year
questions.answer: Take leftover medicine from last year

questions.prompt: Which choice is BEST when you wake up feeling ill?
questions.explain: Doctor + right dose + rest + water is the full safe plan.
options: See a doctor, then rest and drink water
Only sleep all day and skip water
Share leftover pills with a sibling
questions.answer: See a doctor, then rest and drink water

questions.prompt: Name three good things to do when you are ill.
questions.explain: These three help you get better safely.
questions.answer: See a doctor; take the right dose on time; rest and drink water.

questions.prompt: Should you take leftover medicine when you are ill? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Leftover medicine may be wrong or unsafe for you.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Always see a doctor when you feel ill.
questions.answer: doctor
questions.blank: When you are ill, you should see a ____.

questions.prompt: Match SHOULD vs SHOULD NOT when ill.
questions.explain: Doctor, right dose, rest, water — yes. Leftovers and random pharmacy buys — no.

questions.prompt: Which plan is BEST?
questions.explain: See a doctor first. Never take leftover medicine.
options: See a doctor; do not take last winter's syrup
Take the old syrup and skip the doctor
questions.answer: See a doctor; do not take last winter's syrup
questions.story: Merlin has a fever. Mum asks what to do. He also has leftover cough syrup from last winter.

questions.prompt: Resting more and drinking plenty of water is something you ____ when ill.
questions.explain: Rest and water help your body recover — along with seeing a doctor.
options: Only do if you skip the doctor
questions.answer: SHOULD do

questions.prompt: Name one thing you SHOULD NOT do when ill.
questions.explain: No leftover medicine, no random pharmacy buys, and not only sleeping.

facts.why: Both help you, but they check you in different ways and may give different medicine.
facts.can: Explain one difference between a doctor and a Chinese medicine practitioner.
facts.summary: Doctors and Chinese medicine practitioners both check you and prescribe medicine. A doctor uses a stethoscope; a CMP checks your pulse by hand.

questions.prompt: Who uses a stethoscope to check your heartbeat?
questions.explain: A doctor uses a stethoscope. A CMP checks pulse by hand.
options: Both equally use only a stethoscope
questions.answer: A doctor

questions.prompt: Who usually checks your pulse by hand?
questions.explain: CMP checks pulse by hand; doctor uses a stethoscope.
options: A doctor with a stethoscope only
questions.answer: A Chinese medicine practitioner

questions.prompt: What do BOTH a doctor and a Chinese medicine practitioner do?
questions.explain: Same goals; different checking tools and kinds of medicine.
options: Check your condition and prescribe medicine
questions.answer: Check your condition and prescribe medicine

questions.prompt: Match each helper to how they check you.
questions.explain: Same goal (help you), different checking tools.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: The stethoscope helps the doctor hear your heartbeat.
questions.answer: stethoscope
questions.blank: A doctor uses a ____ to listen to your heartbeat.

questions.prompt: What do BOTH a doctor and a Chinese medicine practitioner do?
questions.explain: They both help you get well, even if their methods differ.
questions.answer: Both check your condition and prescribe medicine.

questions.prompt: How does a Chinese medicine practitioner often check you?
questions.explain: They check your pulse by hand.

questions.prompt: Which is TRUE about doctor vs CMP?
questions.explain: Similarities: check + prescribe. Differences: tools and kinds of medicine.
options: They both help, but check you differently and may give different medicine
Only CMPs ever check your condition
questions.answer: They both help, but check you differently and may give different medicine
questions.story: Merlin's uncle says doctors and Chinese medicine practitioners are exactly the same in every way.

questions.prompt: Which statement is NOT true?
questions.explain: Both check your physical condition.
options: A CMP checks pulse by hand
Only a doctor ever checks your condition
questions.answer: Only a doctor ever checks your condition

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Pulse by hand is the CMP difference.
questions.answer: pulse
questions.blank: A Chinese medicine practitioner checks your ____ by hand.

facts.why: The doctor needs to know how you feel so they can give you the right help.
facts.can: Role-play telling a doctor how you feel.
facts.summary: When you visit the doctor, tell them how you feel and follow their instructions.

questions.prompt: When the doctor asks how you feel, you should:
questions.explain: Honest answers help the doctor help you.
options: Tell the doctor how you feel
Say you feel fine even if you do not
questions.answer: Tell the doctor how you feel

questions.prompt: Which is BEST after the doctor gives instructions?
questions.explain: Listen carefully and follow the doctor's plan.
options: Ignore them if you feel shy
Ask a classmate to change them
questions.answer: Pay attention and follow them

questions.prompt: Which is NOT helpful at the clinic?
questions.explain: Hiding symptoms can lead to wrong care.
questions.answer: Hiding your symptoms

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Describe your symptoms clearly.
questions.answer: feel
questions.blank: Tell the doctor how you ____.

questions.prompt: What should Merlin do?
questions.explain: The doctor needs the truth to prescribe the right care.
options: Tell the doctor his tummy hurts
questions.answer: Tell the doctor his tummy hurts
questions.story: At the clinic, Merlin feels shy. His tummy hurts but he does not want to talk.

questions.prompt: After the doctor gives instructions, what should you do?
questions.explain: Follow the doctor's instructions carefully.

questions.prompt: Two important things when seeing the doctor:
questions.explain: Talk honestly and then follow the plan.
questions.answer: Tell how you feel; follow the doctor's instructions.

questions.prompt: Match visit step to action.
questions.explain: Honesty + following instructions = good visit.

questions.prompt: Which reply is BEST?
questions.explain: Clear, honest symptoms help the doctor.
options: My throat hurts and I have a headache
Guess what is wrong without telling
questions.answer: My throat hurts and I have a headache
questions.story: The doctor asks Merlin, 'How do you feel today?' Merlin has a sore throat and headache.

questions.prompt: Should you hide how you feel from the doctor? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Never hide symptoms from the doctor.

facts.why: Medicine can be syrup, pills, Chinese powder or herbs. Only take the right kind for you.
facts.can: Name four types of medicine.
facts.summary: Medicine comes as cough syrup, pills, Chinese medicine powder, and Chinese herbs.

questions.prompt: Which is a liquid type of medicine from the lesson?
questions.explain: Cough syrup is liquid; pills are solid; powder and herbs are other forms.
questions.answer: Cough syrup

questions.prompt: Which form is usually small solid tablets?
questions.explain: Pills are small solid tablets.
questions.answer: Pills

questions.prompt: Chinese medicine powder is BEST described as:
questions.explain: Powder differs from syrup, pills, and whole herbs.
options: Not a medicine type in the lesson
questions.answer: Fine powder medicine (not liquid syrup)

questions.prompt: Match the medicine type to a hint.
questions.explain: Know the forms so you take the correct one.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Cough syrup is liquid medicine.
questions.answer: Cough syrup
questions.blank: ____ is a liquid type of medicine for coughs.

questions.prompt: List four types of medicine from the lesson.
questions.explain: These are the forms in your textbook.
questions.answer: Cough syrup, pills, Chinese medicine powder, Chinese herbs.

questions.prompt: Name one solid form of medicine.
questions.explain: Pills are a common solid form.

questions.prompt: Which is CORRECT?
questions.explain: Syrup, pills, powder, and herbs are all lesson medicine types.
options: All four can be types of medicine from the lesson
Only cough syrup counts as medicine
Herbs are never used as medicine
questions.answer: All four can be types of medicine from the lesson
questions.story: Mum shows Merlin four packages: cough syrup, pills, Chinese powder, and Chinese herbs.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT one of the four medicine types in the lesson?
questions.explain: Water helps you take medicine but is not a medicine type here.
options: Water with no medicine in it
questions.answer: Water with no medicine in it

questions.prompt: Name one Chinese medicine form from the lesson.
questions.explain: Chinese medicine powder or Chinese herbs.

facts.why: The label tells you exactly how to take the medicine safely.
facts.can: Name three things you can find on a medicine label.
facts.summary: The label shows clinic, name, start date/days, amount, how much/when, how to take, and side effects. Never take other people's medicine.

questions.prompt: Your friend offers leftover medicine. You should:
questions.explain: Other people's medicine may be wrong or unsafe for you.
questions.answer: Never take other people's medicine

questions.prompt: Which information is useful on a medicine label?
questions.explain: Labels also show clinic, start date/days, amount, and how to take.
options: Your name, dose, when to take it, and side effects
Only the colour of the bottle
questions.answer: Your name, dose, when to take it, and side effects

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a reason labels are useful?
questions.explain: Labels stop guessing — they give exact instructions.
options: Know how much and when to take
Guess a random dose without reading
questions.answer: Guess a random dose without reading

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Medicine is prescribed for one person only.
questions.answer: people
questions.blank: Never take other ____'s medicine.

questions.prompt: Name three things a medicine label tells you.
questions.explain: Read the whole label before taking medicine.
questions.answer: Your name; dose and time; how to take it / side effects (also clinic, start date, days).

questions.prompt: Should you skip reading the medicine label? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Always read the label so you take the right amount.

questions.prompt: What should Merlin do?
questions.explain: Never take someone else's medicine — ask an adult or doctor.
options: Refuse and ask Mum/Dad or a doctor
questions.answer: Refuse and ask Mum/Dad or a doctor
questions.story: Merlin's sister has a cold. She gives Merlin her cough syrup because he also coughs a little.

questions.prompt: Match label use to reason.
questions.explain: Every label detail keeps you safe.

questions.prompt: Which BEST describes why you check the start date / days?
questions.explain: Start date and days tell the treatment length.
options: To know how long to take the medicine
questions.answer: To know how long to take the medicine

questions.prompt: Name one thing you can find on a medicine label.
questions.explain: Name, dose, timing, side effects, clinic, dates…

facts.why: Taking medicine the right way helps you get better safely.
facts.can: Explain how to take medicine correctly.
facts.summary: Take medicine with water, on time, and follow the doctor. Do not take the wrong amount, stop early, or take others' medicine.

questions.prompt: The BEST way to take medicine is:
questions.explain: Water + right time + doctor's plan = safe.
options: With water, on time, following the doctor
Stop when you feel a bit better
With any drink at any time
questions.answer: With water, on time, following the doctor

questions.prompt: Which is a WRONG way to take medicine?
questions.explain: Wrong amount, stopping early, or others' medicine are wrong.
questions.answer: Take the wrong amount

questions.prompt: You feel better after two days. What should you do?
questions.explain: Do not stop without the doctor's instructions.
options: Give the rest to a friend
questions.answer: Ask the doctor before stopping

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Water is the safe way to swallow medicine.
questions.answer: water
questions.blank: Take medicine with ____.

questions.prompt: Name two WRONG ways to take medicine.
questions.explain: These mistakes can make you worse or unsafe.
questions.answer: Wrong amount; stop without asking the doctor; take other people's medicine.

questions.prompt: If you feel better, can you stop medicine without asking the doctor? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Always ask the doctor before stopping.

questions.prompt: What should Merlin do?
questions.explain: Follow the schedule unless the doctor says otherwise.
options: Take it on time as the doctor said
Skip it because he feels better
questions.answer: Take it on time as the doctor said
questions.story: It is 8 pm — medicine time. Merlin feels a bit better and wants to skip tonight's dose.

questions.prompt: Match action to correct/wrong.
questions.explain: Correct = water, on time, follow doctor.

questions.prompt: Which choice is BEST?
questions.explain: Never take others' medicine; read your own label.
options: Do not take someone else's medicine — check the label
Take the brother's pills if colours match
questions.answer: Do not take someone else's medicine — check the label
questions.story: Merlin almost takes his brother's pills because the bottles look similar.

questions.prompt: Name one CORRECT way to take medicine.
questions.explain: With water, on time, follow the doctor.

facts.why: Bad storage can spoil medicine or make it dangerous for young children.
facts.can: Say where medicine should be kept at home.
facts.summary: Keep medicine in a cool, dry place, away from strong sunlight, and out of reach of young children.

questions.prompt: Where should you store medicine?
questions.explain: Cool, dry, shaded, and out of reach.
options: In a cool, dry place out of children's reach
In strong sunlight by the window
In a damp place young children open
questions.answer: In a cool, dry place out of children's reach

questions.prompt: Which storage place is NOT safe?
questions.explain: Out of reach of young children is required.
options: A high locked cupboard, cool and dry
On a low shelf where toddlers play
A shaded dry cabinet adults use
A cool drawer children cannot open
questions.answer: On a low shelf where toddlers play

questions.prompt: Why keep medicine away from strong sunlight?
questions.explain: Away from strong sunlight keeps medicine good.
options: Heat and light can spoil it
Sunlight is required for all medicine
questions.answer: Heat and light can spoil it

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Moisture can spoil medicine.
questions.answer: dry
questions.blank: Keep medicine in a cool, ____ place.

questions.prompt: Match storage rule to reason.
questions.explain: All three rules keep medicine safe.
pairs: Heat and light can spoil it

questions.prompt: Should medicine be kept where young children can reach it? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Keep it out of reach to prevent accidents.

questions.prompt: Three rules for storing medicine:
questions.explain: Remember: cool, dry, shaded, high/safe.
questions.answer: Cool and dry; away from sunlight; out of young children's reach.

questions.prompt: Which home spot is BEST?
questions.explain: Cool, dry, shaded, out of children's reach.
options: High cool dry cupboard adults control
questions.answer: High cool dry cupboard adults control
questions.story: The family chooses where to put Merlin's medicine bottle.

questions.prompt: Which rule is missing if medicine sits in a sunny wet bathroom kids use?
questions.explain: That spot breaks every storage rule.
options: Cool, dry, away from sun, and out of reach — all missing
Only the colour rule is missing
Only the doctor's name is missing
questions.answer: Cool, dry, away from sun, and out of reach — all missing

questions.prompt: Name one rule for storing medicine.
questions.explain: Cool/dry, away from sun, or out of reach.

facts.why: Rest, water, healthy food and fresh air all help your body fight illness.
facts.can: List four ways to get better when you are ill.
facts.summary: See a doctor soon, take medicine as told, keep home airy, rest, drink water, and eat healthy food.

questions.prompt: Which helps you get better when ill?
questions.explain: Also see a doctor, take medicine as told, keep home airy.
options: Rest, drink water, eat healthy food
Stay in a stuffy closed room only
Play hard outside all day while feverish
questions.answer: Rest, drink water, eat healthy food

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a lesson tip for getting better?
questions.explain: Airy home + rest help recovery.
options: Keep all windows shut forever and skip rest
questions.answer: Keep all windows shut forever and skip rest

questions.prompt: Which plan is BEST for recovery?
questions.explain: All six tips work together.
options: Doctor + medicine as told + airy home + rest + water + healthy food
Only junk food and no rest
questions.answer: Doctor + medicine as told + airy home + rest + water + healthy food

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Healthy food gives your body energy to heal.
questions.answer: healthy
questions.blank: Eat ____ food to help you get better.

questions.prompt: Name four ways to get better faster.
questions.explain: Doctors + rest + fresh air + water + healthy food.
questions.answer: See a doctor; take medicine as told; keep home airy; rest; drink water; eat healthy food.

questions.prompt: Should the home be stuffy or airy when you are ill?
questions.explain: Keep the home airy for fresh air.

questions.prompt: What should Merlin's family do?
questions.explain: Airy home, rest and healthy food support recovery.
options: Open windows a bit, rest, eat healthy food
Only eat junk food and skip rest
questions.answer: Open windows a bit, rest, eat healthy food
questions.story: Merlin has a cold. The windows are shut all day and he only wants junk food.

questions.prompt: Match tip to purpose.
questions.explain: Each tip supports getting well.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT enough by itself?
questions.explain: Airy home helps, but doctor care still matters.
options: Also see a doctor and take medicine as told — window alone is not enough
questions.answer: Also see a doctor and take medicine as told — window alone is not enough
questions.story: Dad says Merlin only needs to open a window and can skip seeing a doctor.

questions.prompt: Name one way to get better when ill.
questions.explain: Any of the six lesson tips.

facts.topic: Caring for someone who is ill
facts.why: Small caring acts make someone who is ill feel loved.
facts.can: Say how you can care for a sick classmate.
facts.summary: Remind them to take medicine, give them a call, and give them a get-well card.

questions.prompt: Your classmate is ill at home. A kind thing to do is:
questions.explain: Call, reminder, or card shows care — not your medicine.
options: Call them and make a get-well card
Give them your own leftover medicine
Invite them to play football right now
questions.answer: Call them and make a get-well card

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a lesson way to care for patients?
questions.explain: Never share medicine; remind, call, or card instead.
questions.answer: Give them your leftover pills

questions.prompt: Which is BEST if your friend is home with flu?
questions.explain: Remind, call, card — simple and kind.
options: Call and send a get-well card; remind them about medicine
Play loud games in their room
Tell them to skip the doctor
questions.answer: Call and send a get-well card; remind them about medicine

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: A get-well card cheers them up.
questions.answer: well
questions.blank: You can make a get-____ card for a sick friend.

questions.prompt: Three ways to care for someone who is ill:
questions.explain: Remind, call, card — simple and kind.
questions.answer: Remind them to take medicine; give a call; give a card.

questions.prompt: Name one way to care for an ill friend.
questions.explain: Call, card, or medicine reminder all count.

questions.prompt: What should Merlin do?
questions.explain: Kind contact helps; do not share medicine.
options: Call Tom and make a get-well card
Ignore Tom until he is better
Shout through the window all night
questions.answer: Call Tom and make a get-well card
questions.story: Tom is home with flu. Merlin wants to help but is not a doctor.

questions.prompt: Match caring act to meaning.
questions.explain: Small acts show big care.
pairs: Help them follow the doctor's plan
Cheer them up with kind words

questions.prompt: Which choice is WORST?
questions.explain: Sharing leftover medicine is unsafe — not true care.
options: Hand Mei leftover medicine from home
Remind Mei to take her prescribed medicine
questions.answer: Hand Mei leftover medicine from home
questions.story: Mei is ill. Classmates suggest ways to help.

questions.prompt: Complete: give a get-____ card.
questions.explain: Get-well card.

chapters.title: Say No to Smoking, Drinking and Drugs

facts.why: Smoking hurts breath, teeth, fingers, appetite, lungs and can cause serious diseases.
facts.can: Name three harms of smoking.
facts.summary: Smoking causes bad breath, yellow fingers and teeth, poor appetite and weight loss, serious diseases, and reduced lung growth.

questions.prompt: Which is a harm of smoking?
questions.explain: Smoking yellows teeth/fingers and causes bad breath.
questions.answer: Bad breath and yellow teeth

questions.prompt: Which harm is more typical of SMOKING than of drinking alcohol?
questions.explain: Yellow fingers/teeth and bad breath are smoking harms; liver/stomach/judgement harms are drinking.
questions.answer: Yellow fingers and teeth

questions.prompt: Which statement about smoking is NOT true?
questions.explain: Smoking reduces lung growth and functions.
options: It reduces lung growth and functions
It can raise chance of serious diseases
It causes poor appetite and weight loss
questions.answer: It makes lungs grow stronger

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Bad breath is an early, clear harm of smoking.
questions.answer: breath
questions.blank: Smoking gives you bad ____.

questions.prompt: Name four harms of smoking.
questions.explain: Smoking hurts many parts of the body.
questions.answer: Bad breath; yellow fingers/teeth; poor appetite and weight loss; serious diseases; reduced lung growth.

questions.prompt: Does smoking help lungs grow well? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Smoking reduces lung growth and function.

questions.prompt: What should Merlin say?
questions.explain: Always refuse. Smoking is harmful.
options: Try one puff to be cool
questions.answer: Say no — smoking harms health
questions.story: An older kid offers Merlin a cigarette and says it looks cool.

questions.prompt: Match smoking harm to body effect.
questions.explain: Smoking harms appearance, appetite, and lungs.

questions.prompt: Which pair BEST lists smoking harms from the lesson?
questions.explain: Those are smoking harms; liver/pass out are drinking; others are other chapters.
options: Bad breath, yellow teeth, reduced lung growth
Liver cancer, stomach bleeding, pass out
questions.answer: Bad breath, yellow teeth, reduced lung growth

questions.prompt: Name one harm of smoking.
questions.explain: Any smoking harm from the lesson.

facts.why: Alcohol hurts your body now and later, and can hurt people around you.
facts.can: Explain why drinking is dangerous for health and safety.
facts.summary: Drinking can make you lose control/judgement or pass out, cause accidents and losses, and later damage brain, heart, liver and stomach.

questions.prompt: Drinking alcohol can make you:
questions.explain: You may lose control, pass out, or cause accidents.
questions.answer: Lose control and judgement

questions.prompt: Which harm is more typical of DRINKING than of smoking?
questions.explain: Drinking: behaviour/safety + brain/heart/liver/stomach. Smoking: breath, teeth, lungs.
questions.answer: Liver cancer and losing judgement

questions.prompt: Which is a long-term HEALTH harm of drinking?
questions.explain: Those are the textbook long-term drinking harms.
options: Brain damage / heart failure / liver cancer / stomach bleeding
questions.answer: Brain damage / heart failure / liver cancer / stomach bleeding

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Say no — drinking harms your health.
questions.answer: no
questions.blank: If someone asks you to drink, say ____.

questions.prompt: Match drinking harm to type.
questions.explain: Drinking harms behaviour now and organs later.

questions.prompt: Name two long-term health harms of drinking.
questions.explain: Organs can be seriously damaged.
questions.answer: Brain damage; heart failure; liver cancer; stomach bleeding.

questions.prompt: What should you say if someone asks you to drink?
questions.explain: Say no clearly.

questions.prompt: Which reply is BEST?
questions.explain: Refuse clearly.
options: Say no — drinking harms my health
Take one sip to be polite
Dare a friend to drink more
questions.answer: Say no — drinking harms my health
questions.story: At a party, someone offers Merlin alcohol and says one sip is fine.

questions.prompt: Losing money or causing accidents after drinking is mainly a ____ danger.
questions.explain: Lose control/judgement/pass out → accidents, harm others, lose things.
questions.answer: Behaviour / safety

questions.prompt: Name one long-term health harm of drinking.
questions.explain: Brain, heart, liver, or stomach harms.

facts.why: Drug abuse is very dangerous: it hurts you, your family and your future.
facts.can: Define drug abuse in your own words.
facts.summary: Drug abuse means taking drugs that may harm body or mind, not for treating illness. It can harm health, studies, appearance, and even cause death.

questions.prompt: Drug abuse means:
questions.explain: Abuse = harmful use, not prescribed treatment.
options: Taking drugs that may harm you, not for treating illness
Taking medicine for illness as the doctor said
questions.answer: Taking drugs that may harm you, not for treating illness

questions.prompt: Which is NOT drug abuse?
questions.explain: Doctor-prescribed treatment is not abuse.
options: Taking prescribed medicine for illness as the doctor said
Taking harmful drugs not for illness
Using drugs that harm body or mind for fun
Taking drugs that may cause death
questions.answer: Taking prescribed medicine for illness as the doctor said

questions.prompt: Which is a long-term effect of drug abuse?
questions.explain: Serious lasting effects including death.
options: Harm studies/work, appearance, health — even death
questions.answer: Harm studies/work, appearance, health — even death

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Not for treating illness = abuse definition.
questions.answer: illness
questions.blank: Drug abuse means taking drugs that may do harm, not for treating ____.

questions.prompt: Name three long-term effects of drug abuse.
questions.explain: Effects are serious and lasting.
questions.answer: Harm self/others; health problems; hurt work/studies; change appearance; death.

questions.prompt: Can drug abuse cause death? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Yes — it can even cause death.

questions.prompt: Which statement is TRUE?
questions.explain: It harms health, studies, appearance — and can kill.
options: Drug abuse can harm studies and health
Trying drugs once is always safe
Drug abuse is good for appearance
questions.answer: Drug abuse can harm studies and health
questions.story: In class, kids debate drugs. Merlin must choose the true idea.

questions.prompt: Match idea to true/false.
questions.explain: Know the definition and the serious effects.

questions.prompt: Which BEST completes: Drug abuse can harm ____.
questions.explain: Wide, serious harm — including death.
options: Yourself, others, studies, appearance, and even cause death
Only yellow teeth like smoking alone
questions.answer: Yourself, others, studies, appearance, and even cause death

questions.prompt: Is taking medicine as the doctor prescribed for illness called drug abuse? (yes/no)
questions.explain: Prescribed treatment is not abuse.

facts.why: Say no, and if others are in danger, get help from an adult or the police.
facts.can: Say what to do if someone offers you drugs.
facts.summary: If offered cigarettes, alcohol or drugs, say no. If others are offered them, tell teachers/parents, call the police, run away, or stop them.

questions.prompt: If someone offers you drugs, you should:
questions.explain: Refuse clearly — then get away and tell an adult if needed.
questions.answer: Say no

questions.prompt: If you see someone offering drugs to classmates, which is BEST?
questions.explain: Tell trusted adults; you may also run away or stop them safely.
options: Tell teachers or parents (or call the police)
Take the drugs to hide them
questions.answer: Tell teachers or parents (or call the police)

questions.prompt: Which action is NOT helpful when drugs appear around you?
questions.explain: Get help — do not stay silent.
options: Pretend nothing is wrong and tell nobody
questions.answer: Pretend nothing is wrong and tell nobody

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank.
questions.explain: Tell trusted adults: teachers or parents.
questions.answer: parents
bank: the person offering drugs to keep it secret
questions.blank: If you see others being offered drugs, tell your teacher or ____.

questions.prompt: Match the situation to the action.
questions.explain: Refuse for yourself; get help for others.

questions.prompt: Four helpful actions if drugs appear around you:
questions.explain: Protect yourself and get adult help.
questions.answer: Say no; tell teachers/parents; call the police; run away / stop them.

questions.prompt: Name one trusted person to tell if someone offers drugs.
questions.explain: Teachers, parents, or the police.

questions.prompt: What should Merlin do?
questions.explain: Get adult help and stay safe.
options: Tell a teacher/parent or call the police; get away
questions.answer: Tell a teacher/parent or call the police; get away
